items.title: DoE terminates coal block auction
items.description: THE DEPARTMENT of Energy (DoE) will no longer pursue its planned coal block auction this year, which would have included the country’s largest mine operated by Semirara Mining and Power Corp. (SMPC).

items.title: Philippine growth seen picking up in second half — World Bank
items.description: PHILIPPINE ECONOMIC growth could pick up in the second half as public infrastructure spending accelerates and inflation eases, bringing the government’s full-year growth target within closer reach, a World Bank economist said.

items.title: OFW remittances in peril amid Middle East war risks
items.description: REMITTANCE FLOWS from overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) are likely to remain subdued until yearend as overseas deployment slows and renewed hostilities in the Middle East create more volatility, banks said.

items.title: NSCR full operations pushed back to 2033
items.description: THE North-South Commuter Railway (NSCR) is now targeted to be fully operational by 2033 after the Economy and Development (ED) Council approved amendments to the project, with partial operations expected to start in December 2027. The full operations of the NSCR are now targeted to start by the third quarter of 2033, later than the […]

items.title: IV of Spades takes top Awit Award nods
items.description: THE four-piece band IV of Spades took home the top prizes — Song of the Year for “Aura” and Album of the Year for Andalucia — at this year’s Awit Awards which were held on Sept. 15 at the SM Mall of Asia Arena in Pasay City. Another track, “Monster,” won Best Sound Engineer Recording.

items.title: Banks’ assets grow at end-July
items.description: ASSETS held by the Philippine banking industry expanded by over 10% year on year as of end-July, driven by sustained growth in lending and deposits, preliminary data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) showed.

items.title: NGCP eyes completion of P23.5-B grid projects
items.description: THE National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) is targeting the completion of six transmission projects worth about P23.5 billion by yearend as the grid operator works to address transmission reliability amid power supply constraints. At a briefing on Thursday, NGCP Assistant Vice-President Cynthia P. Alabanza said the company had already completed five transmission projects […]

items.title: Philippines not ready for AI use in capital markets
items.description: PHILIPPINE CAPITAL markets are not ready for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for trading, advising, or prediction as the country’s investor base remains hesitant about new technologies, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) said. “Customers are resistant to the use [of AI in capital markets]. They’re hesitant, I think. They’re hesitant to use it […]

items.title: Toyota PHL expects vehicle output to fall this year
items.description: TOYOTA MOTOR Philippines Corp. (TMP) expects vehicle production to decline this year amid softer market demand that the automaker linked to higher oil prices stemming from the Middle East conflict. “It’s lower this year at maybe close to 60,000. Last year was about 63,000,” TMP Senior Vice-President for Marketing Division Sherwin T. Chua Lim said […]

items.title: Life insurers cover more than 50% of Filipinos
items.description: THE LIFE insurance industry covered more than half of the Philippine population as of the first half, driven by its growing branch and agency network. The Philippine Life Insurance Association, Inc. (PLIA) said in a statement that the sector now covers 63.5 million Filipinos, equivalent to around 55% of the country’s population. This was supported […]

items.title: Stuff to Do (09/18/26)
items.description: THE Design Center of the Philippines is marking a decade of the International Design Conference (IDC) with its 10th edition on Sept. 18 at the Foro de Intramuros, City of Manila, bringing together leading voices from the Philippines and around the world to look at how design can respond to the complexity and diversity of the world we live in.

items.title: SEC urges finance executives to help bring more firms to capital market
items.description: THE Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has urged financial executives to introduce more Philippine companies to the capital market earlier in their growth, as the country continues to lag regional peers in the number of listed firms and has yet to record an initial public offering (IPO) this year. SEC Chairperson Francisco Ed. Lim said […]

items.title: Are we ready for the next wave of global capital?
items.description: There is a revealing question behind the Philippines’ latest foreign direct investment numbers: are we failing to attract capital, or are we failing to prepare for the kind of capital that will shape the next economy? The distinction matters. The 2026 Global Atlas of Risk and Readiness (GARR) gives us a useful place to begin. […]

items.title: Finance runs on trust
items.description: At its most basic, the financial system performs a simple but indispensable function: it moves funds from those who have an excess of them to those who need them. Households place savings in banks. Banks transform deposits into loans. Investors provide capital to businesses. Pension funds convert workers’ savings into long-term investments. items.title: 29% of hotel rooms expected by 2026 canceled — report
items.description: NEARLY three in 10 hotel rooms that had been projected two years ago to open by 2026 were canceled, even as the country’s current accommodation pipeline has grown to P387 billion through 2032. items.title: Peso inches up as oil prices ease
items.description: THE PESO edged higher against the dollar on Thursday as oil prices continued to go down on easing supply concerns. The currency gained 0.9 centavo to end at P62.73 versus the greenback from its P62.739 finish on Wednesday, according to Bankers Association of the Philippines data. The local unit opened Thursday’s session weaker at P62.83 […]

items.title: Migratory birds offer a natural flight path to growth and resilience
items.description: SOME of the world’s most valuable infrastructure has no owner, no border, and no name most people would recognize. It’s the network of wetlands that keeps migratory birds alive during their odysseys across the planet.

items.title: Nestlé says Philippines remains among top growth markets
items.description: SWISS food and beverage company Nestlé S.A. said the Philippines remains one of its top growth markets globally, citing demand for its brands and the country’s demographic and economic conditions. items.description: VISA has expanded offerings for its Visa Infinite cards, adding two new tiers with expanded access to more personalized experiences centered around lifestyle and travel amid strong payments growth in the affluent segment. “In a consumption-driven economy such as the Philippines, payments continue to shape how people dine, travel, shop, and pursue their passions. items.description: Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries. Business models are evolving faster than ever. items.title: Animal Law takes center stage as first Philippine conference calls for stronger protection and accountability
items.description: Animal welfare in the Philippines is entering a new phase as lawmakers, government officials, lawyers, veterinarians, law enforcement officers, local and national government representatives, regulatory agencies, advocates, and young leaders gathered for the country’s first Philippine Animal Law Conference, calling for stronger laws, effective enforcement, and greater accountability for the protection of animals. items.title: PHL labor market ‘resilient’ in face of AI boom
items.description: THE PHILIPPINE labor market and services exports are highly exposed to artificial intelligence (AI), but remain largely resilient as the technology has so far only transformed jobs rather than eliminated them, ING Bank N.V. said.  “While the Philippines is among the economies most exposed to AI-driven change, the evidence so far points to job transformation […]

items.title: On schadenfreude
items.description: The 19th century German philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer once described schadenfreude as an expression of envy or resentment. It is the taking of malicious pleasure in another individual’s misery. The sensation is something many people feel when an unfortunate thing happens to someone, especially if that person seems to have it all. Although the word has […]

items.title: The 20th set of Superbods is chosen
items.description: CENTURY TUNA has named Austin Dizon and Vienne Luna as the Grand Winners of the 20th Century Tuna Superbods, chosen from a lineup of 40 finalists.

items.title: Filinvest Land moves to dissolve three subsidiaries
items.description: FILINVEST Land, Inc. (FLI) is moving to dissolve three wholly owned subsidiaries as part of efforts to streamline its corporate structure, while saying the move will not have a material impact on its operations. items.title: More Pinoy couples use contraceptives – CPD
items.description: The number of Filipino couples engaging in family planning through the use of contraceptives is increasing, the Commission on Population and Development said.

items.title: Ridon, Tolosa ordered: Explain sub judice breach
items.description: The Senate impeachment court has ordered Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon and private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. to explain their perceived violations of the court’s sub judice rule.

items.title: Evidence enough to convict VP, says prosecution
items.description: Documentary and testimonial evidence against impeached Vice President Sara Duterte are enough to convict her regardless of whether the conviction threshold is maintained or not, according to the prosecution team of the House of Representatives.

items.title: Palace questions VP Sara’s capability to lead Philippines
items.description: Malacañang questioned the capability of Vice President Sara Duterte to lead the country after her camp claimed she is ready to succeed President Marcos.

items.title: ASEAN ministers sign Manila declaration on disaster management
items.description: Association of Southeast Asian Nations member states have signed the Manila Declaration, affirming their collective commitment to accelerating implementation of the ASEAN Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response Work Programme 2026-2030; strengthening ASEAN accountability, monitoring, and learning for disaster resilience; and shaping the region’s disaster resilience agenda toward 2030 and beyond.

items.title: Growing Chinese surveillance in Philippines waters flagged
items.description: A maritime advocacy group has warned authorities of the increasing number of Chinese research vessels within Philippine waters, and called on the government not to ignore the development.

items.title: Marcos pushes release of class suspension guidelines
items.description: President Marcos wants the updated guidelines on class suspensions during weather disturbances and calamities fast-tracked to prevent confusion among parents and students, Malacañang said yesterday.

items.title: Palace backs SC stance on political dynasty bill
items.description: Malacañang agrees with the Supreme Court on the need to pass a bill banning political dynasties, saying the measure remains a priority of the Marcos administration.

items.title: Senate warned over revising impeachment vote threshold
items.description: Senators acting as judges in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte may face legal challenge including criminal cases if they proceed with changing the two-thirds voting requirement for her conviction, according to former presidential spokesman Salvador Panelo.

items.title: 8 Metro Manila hospitals reach full capacity for leptospirosis
items.description: Eight hospitals in Metro Manila have reached their full capacity for designated leptospirosis beds, the Department of Health reported yesterday.
